the-registry-page-generated-from-the-cha.text: The registry page, generated from the chain.
Ticket #503, a vertical slice of the join-by-token plan. Read the plan for the slices and the touch list for the files. Base: main at e7b55ac9.

story.text: As Alice, I have a registry's state token and the packaged release, and nothing else: no wallet file of mine, nothing from the person who created the registry. I run singular registry describe --state-token … and read a page that says which registry this is, which release it runs, what its rules are and what it holds now. I run it with --json and a program reads the same facts. Everything on the page comes from the public history of the state token and from the release; nothing is typed by hand. I can start Demo 1 from this page.
As Bob, I run the same command on my own machine. If we read the same chain state with the same release, my page and Alice's are the same bytes.

As an integrator, I want to know what the page does not prove. The page says so itself: the indexer's answers are unverified claims, the release label is the archive's own claim, and the page is unsigned.

what-the-page-shows.text: The page carries no clock, no chain tip and no session identity, so identical inputs give identical bytes. Pending requests appear in one fixed order. The text and the JSON carry the same fields.

requirements.text: page-from-chain-and-release-alone: the command takes the state token, the blueprint of the packaged release, a provider and a network. It takes no wallet, no signing key, no state directory and no file of any actor. Any other setting is refused by name before anything is read.
page-reads-and-writes-nothing: no signature, no submission, no journal, no lock and no file under a state directory. The two-actor journey shows the actor's home unchanged after a page.

page-state-equals-public-replay: root, counts, last fold and pending requests equal what a separate public readback of the same chain state shows (the journey compares the page with inspect and with the fold receipts, after each actor's own lifecycle).
page-bytes-identical-for-identical-input: the same replayed history and the same release give the same text and the same JSON, byte for byte, across runs.

page-names-its-release-or-refuses: the version label is read from version.txt beside the blueprint. A missing, unreadable or malformed version.txt is refused by name, with no label. A blueprint that derives a state script hash other than the token's is refused by name.

page-limits-are-stated-not-claimed: the page's provenance line states that it shows only state fields from a checked replay and claims nothing beyond them; provider answers are labelled unverified, the release label is labelled the archive's claim, and the page is labelled unsigned. No limit is written by hand: the page links to the documentation of the claimed version.
release-archive-carries-its-version: the on-chain release archive stages version.txt beside its blueprint and the release check refuses an archive whose version, asset name or checksum disagree.

named-refusals.text: A refusal prints one JSON receipt on standard output with a non-zero exit status, as every command does. A success prints the page, and nothing else.

not-in-the-first-pull-request.text: Not in the first pull request.

Two lines of the issue are on the Demo 1 path and are delivered by a second pull request of this ticket, planned in the plan: create prints the working describe command, and describe runs from the extracted release archive against a node, with Demo 1's run page starting from the page. Three lines are accepted follow-ups, listed with their reason in the plan: a block anchor for the last fold, documentation links verified against a published asset, and the independently derived action identity in the public conformance report. The issue stays open until they are delivered or ruled.

model-binding.text: Lean source 20b35407c8a8e955dea396e59ae926b7c9e13d03, model tree d9161edd0274b67151f331949521f34bbf18612f, constitution 1.15.0. Lean states the registry state, its eight-field configuration, the leaf kinds and the root, and proves that a fold is built from the public view. It has no report command. The page shows only state fields from a checked replay and claims nothing beyond them: the desk ruled this a page with no Lean row and not a stop condition. The page's provenance line says exactly that, in fixed text: the facts are state fields read from a replay checked from create, the indexer's answers are unverified, the release label is the archive's own claim, and the page is unsigned. The count of active and terminal keys is the number of keys whose replayed leaf is active or terminal. No Lean change, no validator change and no blueprint change.
